properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 12 at 12:31AM MST until October 12 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms are expected to
continue across the are through tonight. With tropical moisture
in place from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel and already
saturated grounds, periods of embedded heavy rainfall will be
possible which could lead to flash flooding. Additionally, the
extended period of rain could lead to elevated flow in creeks,
normally dry washes, and rivers.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Tutuila and Aunuu; Manua; Swains Island; Rose Atoll
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 11 at 7:58PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by midweek. This trough should remain
strong and active while over the territory, and may even intensify
with embedded low pressure centers. Widespread showers may be
heavy and persistent at times with the possibility of
thunderstorms. Widespread flash flooding may occur from this
rainfall, and landslides will be possible along steep mountainous
terrain. Impacts could begin as early as Wednesday and are
expected to persist through the weekend. While there is still
uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall, plan
now for wet conditions that could start as early as Wednesday and
persist through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Wednesday through Sunday

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 12 at 2:38AM EDT until October 12 at 5:45AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Delaware County in southeastern Pennsylvania...
Southern Philadelphia County in southeastern Pennsylvania...

* Until 545 AM EDT.

* At 238 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Philadelphia, Yeadon, Folcroft, Swarthmore, East Lansdowne, South
Philadelphia, Roxborough, Morris Park, Center City, Darby Township,
Philadelphia International Airport and Kensington.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 476 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 6 and 7.
Interstate 76 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 340 and 351.
Interstate 95 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 8 and 30.
Interstate 676 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 0 and 1.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 10:35PM MDT until October 12 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm
Rachel will continue to impact the region. While this is expected
to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered instances of
heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger storms yielding
flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and prior burn
scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 11 at 9:02PM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding can be expected near times of high tide. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet
is expected with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon
with normal tidal ranges. Low lying areas will be most
susceptible, including Oceano. Enhanced beach erosion is
likely. The risk for significant damage is very low. There is
an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to be around 7
feet on Monday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 8:45PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, increased risk of rip currents and sneaker waves
expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 1:29PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
As Invest 96W continues to slowly organize and strengthen north of
Kosrae/east of Pohnpei, inflow into the developing disturbance will
allow for locally heavy rainfall to develop, with over 1 inch per
hour rain rates probable from time to time. Rainfall totals will
likely be 2 to 5 inches tonight through Wednesday, with locally
higher amounts possible.

Winds will also increase as 96W strengthens, and at least isolated
wind gusts to 35 knots are possible with any heavy shower or
thunderstorm that develops.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues. Also keep up to date with the latest
information from your local emergency management agency.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS TONIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY, POSSIBLY LONGER

continue to be possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central

northward, impacting portions of east-central and eastern Nevada
through roughly Monday. This significant moisture will interact
with upper level low pressure to bring widespread showers with
isolated thunderstorms to the watch area. Moderate to locally
heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and may result in rock,
mud, and debris flows in and near former fire burned areas, steep
terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Central Henderson County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding around greater Hendersonville.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 535 PM EDT, Mud and Bat Fork Creeks remained in flood and
flooding will continue all afternoon.  The Mud Creek river gage
on North Main Street was nearing 16 feet which indicates flooding
of portions of William H King Memorial Park and the Oklawaha
Greenway.  The river has crested in Hendersonville, but will not
fall below flood stage until late evening or overnight tonight.

local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few inches of water
can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water can sweep your
vehicle away.

Valley Hill and East Flat Rock.

properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Cape May and Atlantic Coastal Cape May.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 2 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 11 at 12:25PM MDT until October 12 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy wet snow occurring. Additional snow accumulations
between 3 and 5 inches. Winds gusting as high as 30 mph.

* WHERE...Melville Foothills.

* WHEN...Until noon MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Recreation in the high
country will be impacted by heavy accumulating snow.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For the latest road conditions, call
5 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: South-Central Shasta County Including Redding Metro; Northern Sacramento Valley in Tehama County; Central Glenn County Including Interstate 5
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 11 at 7:38AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 AM PDT MONDAY DUE TO
WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SHASTA METRO, N. SAC VALLEY IN
TEHAMA COUNTY, AND CENTRAL GLENN CO & INTERSTATE 5...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 124, 142, and 144.

* TIMING...Until 5 AM PDT Monday.

* WINDS...North to northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to
30-40 mph. Strongest winds expected Sunday morning.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 15 to 25 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.
